title: Engineering All-Hands - 2026-04-08
content:
Agenda:
- Quick metrics + health (SLA, P99 latency, error rates)
- Major releases & rollouts (Hosted API, Dedicated autoscaler)
- Incident review: 2026-04-06 KV cache regression
- Private deployment roadmap update
- Console & observability milestones
- Cross-team asks and upcoming cooldowns
- Q&A + shoutouts

Summary/Toplines:
- Production health remains stable: overall 7d avg P99 generation latency 210ms (down 6% week-over-week). Token cost per 1k tokens improved ~4% after batching/quantization policy changes.
- We had a regression on 2026-04-06 tied to KV cache eviction policy that impacted ~1.5% of Hosted API requests for ~45 minutes; root cause identified and mitigated (see incident notes below).
- Dedicated autoscaler v2 rollouts are in progress; internal beta looks good. Target GA: 2026-05-05.
- Private deployment: first on-prem pilot confirmed for a financial customer; infra checklist and compliance docs in progress.

Metrics and health details:
- Latency: 7d avg P50: 42ms, P90: 128ms, P99: 210ms.
- Error rates: API 5xx at 0.08% (baseline target <0.1%), streaming disconnects at 0.15% (up from 0.09% last week, investigating network flaky nodes).
- Throughput: peak concurrent requests per region: us-west-2 18k, eu-central-1 9k.
- Cost: per-token unit costs improved after auto-batching heuristics; still seeing hotspots on small request sizes - PR coming to suggest client-side batching guidance.

Recent launches & rollouts:
- Hosted API: merged PRs to add structured output hints for function calling (GH PR #2147 merged 2026-04-03). Gradual enablement to tiered customers next week.
- Dedicated autoscaler v2: feature flags enabled for internal tenants; metrics show 22% better GPU utilization in steady-state. Still tuning cooldown/window parameters.
- Console: trace view now surfaces token-level cost breakdown (internal flag). UX polish planned for 2 weeks.

Incident review - 2026-04-06 KV cache regression:
- Symptom: sudden spike in generation latency + small increase in 5xx for some model shards between 10:12-10:58 UTC.
- Impact: ~1.5% of hosted API traffic saw degraded P99s and occasional OOM retries; several customers reported longer response times.
- Root cause: a regression in eviction ordering when combining prefix cache and recent-KV merges; caused slightly higher memory churn and higher GC frequency on affected runtime nodes.
- Mitigation: rolled back the KV merge heuristic (hotfix) at 10:47 UTC; traffic returned to baseline by 10:58.
- Action items:
  * Revert was safe; need better canary checks for memory/GC signals (owner: Chen Li, due: 2026-04-15).
  * Add synthetic workload that exercises prefix+merge paths to CI (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-04-12).
  * Post-mortem draft in Confluence; please add any missing customer impact details (link above).

Team highlights / updates:
- Serving runtime:
  * Attention kernel improvements continue - next micro-benchmark cycle shows 7% improvement for long context (2k+ tokens).
  * Working on a new KV sharding config to reduce cross-shard lookups; prototype landed in repo under feature/kv-shard-optim (Rafael).
- Platform engineering:
  * Autoscaler v2 telemetry added to metrics dashboard; need SRE to review resource throttling thresholds.
  * Cluster autoscaling playbook updated for node preemption scenarios.
- Console & Observability:
  * Token-level cost breakdown landed behind feature flag. Need product review for rollout messaging (Maya).
  * Traces: adding deeper function-call traces to help debugging tool-calls (partial rollout this week).
- Private deployments:
  * On-prem pilot with finance customer scheduled for initial deployment window 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-22. Compliance checklist 80% complete. (Owner: Priya Shah in solutions-eng).

Roadmap checkpoints & upcoming milestones:
- 2026-04-15: Canaries for autoscaler v2 expanded to 50% of Dedicated pool.
- 2026-04-22: Console rollout for token-cost visible to all internal teams (feature flag off).
- 2026-05-05: Dedicated autoscaler v2 GA (tentative).
- 2026-05-18: First Private on-prem pilot signoff (pending security review).

Cross-team asks / blockers:
- SRE: please review new autoscaler throttling thresholds and confirm safe limits (ticket JIRA-ENG-3124). Owner: Tomas Becker.
- Product: need copy review for token-cost messaging and potential API doc changes to explain structured output behavior. Owner: Maya Rodriguez.
- Security: final approval for pilot on-prem package - outstanding: HSM/KMS integration test (owner: Chen Li).

Open questions / discussion items:
- How aggressive should we be with default batching heuristics vs. client guidance? Balancing latency-sensitive requests vs. per-token cost. Suggestion: expose a new client hint header for latency-priority. (Discuss in eng-runtime sync 2026-04-09).
- Rollout cadence: autoscaler GA date is ambitious; do we want longer internal bake? Feedback requested from Product/SRE.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Chen Li: add GC/memory signals to canary suite + implement alerting thresholds (due 2026-04-15).
- Liam O'Connor: synthetic CI workload for prefix+merge KV path (due 2026-04-12).
- Maya Rodriguez: copy review for console token-cost messaging (due 2026-04-14).
- Priya Shah: finalize compliance docs for on-prem pilot (due 2026-04-16).
- Rafael Gomez: complete KV sharding prototype tests and bench results (due 2026-04-20).

Shoutouts:
- Big thanks to the runtime on-call (Sandeep + team) for quick detection and rollback on 4/6.
- Serving runtime team for landing the long-context attention micro-optimizations.

AOB / FYI:
- Reminder: engineering-wide code freeze 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-03 for infra migration window. Plan and window exceptions need to be submitted to release-eng.
- Weekly deep-dive: next week we'll have a short demo of autoscaler v2 internal metrics - please RSVP in the calendar invite.

Notes to self / draft points:
- Add link to customer incident reports as they come in.
- Consider small retrospective with on-call post-incident to collect quick wins for runbook.

If you have questions or want to add items to next week's agenda, ping #eng-all or drop a note in this doc.
